brief.headline: Push for a 76% price cut to ₹250/kg — Silk Polypack already sells identical laminate at that level, and the open market confirms ₹205–305/kg is fair

priceAsk.summary: Ask Huhtamaki to match ₹250/kg for the LAMINATE SKU
priceAsk.target: ₹250.00/KG (down from ₹1067.36/KG) — a 76% reduction that saves us ₹58850 per year
priceAsk.basis: Silk Polypack already supplies us identical pharma/ORS sachet laminate at ₹250/kg. The open market asking price for this material sits at ₹205–305/kg, with ₹250/kg typical — so our best price is market-fair. Huhtamaki's ₹1067.36/kg is 326.9% higher than what we pay elsewhere for the same thing

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 days after receipt — no reason to speed up payment when the price gap is this wide

brief.financialLeverage: Huhtamaki is a large, stable listed company with ₹2758.00 Cr in sales and healthy profit — they keep about ₹5 of every ₹100 they sell. They carry almost no debt (0.11x). They're growing fast — sales up 24.0% per year — so they want new orders. But we're tiny to them: our ₹76850 spend is 0.00% of their revenue, which means we have almost no individual pull. The real leverage is the price gap and our willingness to shift all volume to Silk Polypack or another converter if Huhtamaki won't move.

evidence.point: We pay Silk Polypack ₹250/kg for the same laminate
Huhtamaki charges us ₹1067.36/kg — over four times more
The gap is 326.9%, costing us an extra ₹58850 every year
Open-market asking price for pharma/ORS sachet laminate runs ₹205–305/kg, with ₹250/kg typical — so our Silk price is market-fair
Huhtamaki's sales are growing 24.0% per year, so they're hungry for volume
We're only 0.00% of their ₹2758.00 Cr revenue — too small to move them on relationship alone

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant with ₹16492.00 Cr revenue — makes both film and finished laminates, so can supply at scale and benchmark costs across the value chain

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, specialises in pharma blister and sachet laminates — ₹222.04 Cr revenue, already serving pharma customers in India

alternates.name: Amcor Flexibles India Pvt Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Indian arm of global Amcor — known for high-end pharma laminates, very reliable quality (no public revenue data, so financials unknown)

risks: Huhtamaki may refuse to cut 76% in one jump — be ready to walk if they won't come close to ₹250/kg, because staying at ₹1067.36/kg makes no sense when Silk delivers the same material at a quarter of the price

We're 0.00% of their sales, so they may not care if we leave — that's why lining up UFLEX, Constantia or Amcor as a second source (and telling Huhtamaki we're doing it) is critical to show we're serious

If Huhtamaki's ₹1067.36/kg price includes special pharma certifications, packaging or logistics that Silk doesn't provide, ask them to break out those costs line by line — otherwise the gap looks like pure markup
Their sales are growing fast (24.0%/yr) and they're profitable, so they're not desperate — frame the ask as a volume opportunity (we can commit more if the price is right) rather than a squeeze
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to grow our laminate volume with you, but right now we're paying you ₹1067 per kilo when the same material costs us ₹250 from Silk Polypack — can you help us understand that gap and work toward the ₹250 level?
